Class MinHeap<T extends Comparable<T>>

java.lang.Object
assignments.datastructures.MinHeap<T>
Type Parameters:
T - the type of elements, ordered by compareTo
All Implemented Interfaces:
adt.PriorityQueue<T>, adt.Tree<T>, Iterable<T>
public class MinHeap<T extends Comparable<T>> extends Object implements adt.PriorityQueue<T>, adt.Tree<T>
A complete binary min-heap stored in the course's Vector class. Every parent is less than or equal to its children according to natural ordering. Duplicate values are allowed, but null values are not.

Priority-queue operations enqueue and dequeue() take O(log N) amortized time; peek(), isEmpty(), length(), degree(), and height() take O(1) time. Each traversal takes O(N) time and returns an iterator over a snapshot of the tree. The heap's shape is a complete binary tree, but unlike a binary search tree its inorder traversal is not necessarily sorted.

All operations and traversals are iterative; no recursion is used.

      public void enqueue(T value)
      Inserts a value, then moves it upward until heap order is restored. Runs in O(log N) amortized time with a dynamically resized Vector.
      Specified by:

      Parameters:

      Throws:

    • dequeue

      public T dequeue()
      Removes and returns the smallest value. Replaces the root with the final Vector element and iteratively moves it downward as needed. Runs in O(log N) amortized time.
      Specified by:
      dequeue in interface adt.PriorityQueue<T extends Comparable<T>>
      Returns:
      the minimum value
      Throws:
      NoSuchElementException - if the heap is empty

    • degree

      public int degree()
      Returns the maximum number of children of any node in O(1) time. A complete binary tree has degree 0 for at most one node, degree 1 for exactly two nodes, and degree 2 for at least three nodes.
      Specified by:
      degree in interface adt.Tree<T extends Comparable<T>>
      Returns:
      0, 1, or 2, depending on the number of elements

    • height

      public int height()
      Computes height in number of node levels in O(1) time. An empty heap has height 0; a heap with one node has height 1.
      Specified by:
      height in interface adt.Tree<T extends Comparable<T>>
      Returns:
      the number of levels in the complete binary tree

    • inorder

      public Iterator<T> inorder()
      Visits left subtree, root, then right subtree using an explicit stack. Does not necessarily produce sorted values in a min-heap. Runs in O(N) time and returns a snapshot iterator.
      Specified by:
      inorder in interface adt.Tree<T extends Comparable<T>>
      Returns:
      an iterator in inorder (left-root-right)

    • postorder

      public Iterator<T> postorder()
      Visits left subtree, right subtree, then root using an explicit stack and the last completed subtree's index. No recursion is used. Runs in O(N) time and returns a snapshot iterator.
      Specified by:
      postorder in interface adt.Tree<T extends Comparable<T>>
      Returns:
      an iterator in postorder (left-right-root)

    • levelorder

      public Iterator<T> levelorder()
      Visits nodes level by level, left to right. This is the same order as the underlying Vector and needs no extra traversal stack or queue. Runs in O(N) time and returns a snapshot iterator.
      Specified by:
      levelorder in interface adt.Tree<T extends Comparable<T>>
      Returns:
      an iterator in level order (breadth-first order)

    • iterator

      public Iterator<T> iterator()
      Returns a level-order snapshot iterator as the default tree iteration. Unlike a search tree, a heap has no inherently sorted traversal order.
      Specified by:
      iterator in interface Iterable<T extends Comparable<T>>
